question: The unit for specific gravity is _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __no unit (dimensionless)**(Specific Gravity)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Specific Gravity__ is a dimensionless quantity.
 
• It is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference substance, typically water.
 
• Specific gravity has no units because it is a ratio of two similar quantities.
 
• The reference substance used is usually water at 4°C, where its density is 1 g/cm³.
 
• Specific gravity is often used in engineering, physics, and geology to characterize materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Density:**
 
 
• Density is defined as mass per unit volume.
 
• It is expressed in units such as g/cm³ or kg/m³.
 
 
 
• **Relative Density:**
 
 
• Relative density is another term for specific gravity.
 
• It is a dimensionless quantity representing the ratio of densities.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Specific gravity is used in soil testing, fluid mechanics, and material identification.
 
• It helps determine whether a substance will sink or float in a given liquid.
